title: Greedy score-density packing under a token budget, with per-type floors
summary: (1 − 1/e)-optimal for the submodular objective MMR induces, which is good enough that exact knapsack is not worth its complexity.
description:
Replace count-based selection with budget-constrained packing: greedily select by `score / tokens` under a caller-supplied `max_tokens`, subject to the existing `min_results_by_type` floors as hard constraints. Exact 0/1 knapsack is O(n·B) and affordable at our scale, but the greedy bound (Nemhauser, Wolsey & Fisher 1978) is strong enough that the exact solver would be complexity without benefit — record that reasoning in the docstring so it is not relitigated.

Preserve `_relevant_with_backfill()` semantics: floors are satisfied first, then the remaining budget is packed by density.

Acceptance: cards respect `max_tokens` and never exceed it; per-type floors are honoured even under tight budgets, or the call fails loudly rather than silently dropping a floor; measured against the existing suite reporting both quality and token count; `max_tokens=None` reproduces current behaviour exactly. Depends on ASMB-1 and RTRV-5.
